correctness.rationale: In named-identity ternary RELATIONAL multiplication, all two-variable atoms reduce by cancellation to x=1,y=1,x=y,x²=1,y²=1,y=x²,x=y²,xy=1. With one nonidentity anchor of order prime p, exceptional replies are 1,a,a²,a^{-1},a^{(p+1)/2}, with coincidences for p=2,3; generic reply available exactly in six stated classes, independent of anchor even for nonabelian groups. This uniformly available extension-profile set is a permanent two-pebble bisimulation, hence handles all FO² quantifier depths (not an extrapolation from two rounds). Four explicit FO² sentence tests separate all six classes. Independently enumerated all ternary atomic diagrams and either-pebble replacement sets for ten calibration groups, including nonabelian Heisenberg H3/H5.
residual_risks: Finite calibration cannot prove all groups/primes; symbolic power identities and invariant-anchor argument do.

originality.rationale: The Oct 26 all-prime-exponent-groups theorem explicitly proves the identical six classes and stronger uniform pointed extension-profile lemmas for EVERY nonidentity anchor (including nonabelian groups). The Nov 2 complete unbounded-FO² classification for elementary abelian prime groups spells out the standard permanent two-pebble back-and-forth from precisely such uniform profiles. Combining these published proof ingredients yields unbounded-depth equivalence for the same six classes; no new group-specific obstruction, profile, or distinction is introduced.
